assumptions: Tỷ VND; nghìn visits. Bệnh viện hư cấu Tường Vi. Toy shared diagnostic expense allocated theo verified test counts, central overhead not allocated. Payer reimbursement already net. All direct expenses include staff; no tax.

evidence.text:
[Bảng dịch vụ]
|Line|Visits nghìn|Net fee triệu/visit|Direct cost tỷ|Diagnostic tests nghìn|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|Cardiology|20|2.5|30|12|
|Orthopedic|15|3.0|28|8|
|General|30|1.2|24|10|
[Chi phí chung] Diagnostic lab cash-type expense 18 tỷ, phân bổ theo test count. Central admin 15 tỷ ngoài lab, không allocate theo service line.
[KPI] Service-line contribution = earned revenue − direct cost − allocated lab. Group EBIT subtracts all lab and central. Không depreciation khác.
[Cash] Total patient/payer collections 125, opening AR 15; all earned invoiced. Direct/lab/admin actual cash payment not supplied.
[Draft] CFO assigns lab cost by visits, allocating 20% lab cost to general because lower average fee. No actual approved allocation change.
[Clinical note] Visits not adjusted for patient acuity, outcomes or complexity.

qas.question: Find earned cardiology service revenue.
Find diagnostic lab cost allocated to Orthopedic under the approved method.
Find General contribution after its allocated lab expense.
Find group operating result after central administration.
Find ending patient and payer AR on net earned amounts.
Explain why reallocation of the same lab cost cannot improve total group EBIT.
qas.answer: A change in attribution reallocates the existing 18b across service lines but does not change total resources consumed. Group cost remains 18b.

qas.question: Is low General margin a sufficient reason to discontinue that service?
qas.answer: No. Allocated lab costs may not be avoidable, and clinical/community obligations and patient outcomes are outside the toy.

qas.question: Can case-mix-adjusted cost per visit be measured?
qas.answer: No. Acuity and clinical complexity are not quantified.

qas.question: Find closing truck PPE carrying from asset movement table.
Find net disposal gain for the whole fleet.

qas.question: Can direct cost per loaded km be presented as total-km efficiency?

qas.question: Can fuel efficiency in liters per tonne-km be computed?

assumptions: Tỷ VND. Nhà mạng giả lập Đồi Mây. Toy spectrum license amortization straight-line by remaining lives and ready-for-use timing; renewal deposits are refundable assets, no extension until approval. No tax.

evidence.text:
[License table]
|Band|Opening carrying|Remaining life Jan1|Addition|Ready date of addition|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
|700 MHz|400|8 years|0|—|
|1800 MHz|240|4 years|0|—|
|3500 MHz|0|—|600|July1|
[New license] 3500 MHz life 15 years, full 600 cash paid. No residual, impairment or disposal.
[Renewal] Refundable application deposit 30 cash for 1800 MHz pending renewal, held as separate deposit asset. No regulator approval yet, remaining original life unchanged.
[P&L] Service revenue 2.000; cash-type opex 1.300; network depreciation 250, spectrum amortization not included. Interest 80; no tax.
[Cash] CFO before interest 450; interest cash CFO, network capex cash 300. Spectrum purchase and application deposit investing cash. No new debt or other flows.
[Draft] CTO capitalizes deposit in 1800 MHz, extends its useful life and records full-year amortization for new 3500 band.

qas.question: Find current 700MHz license amortization.
Find first-year amortization of 3500MHz license from July1.
Find total current spectrum amortization across the three bands.
Find total closing spectrum intangible carrying, excluding refundable deposit.
Find PBT after both network depreciation and spectrum amortization.
Explain why the refundable 30b deposit cannot justify a longer license life.
qas.answer: It is a separate refundable payment, not an approved renewal; original legal/usage life remains unchanged under the toy.

qas.question: Does the 600b license purchase equal current spectrum expense?
qas.answer: No. It is a capital addition; current expense for the new license is only 20b amortization.

qas.question: Can the value of the pending renewal be assessed from the deposit amount?
qas.answer: No. The deposit does not establish renewal price, terms or approval likelihood.

assumptions: Triệu USD; million ASK, RPK, tonne-km. Hãng hư cấu Hạc Lam. Toy allocate common aircraft cash cost by specified passenger/cargo weight; separate direct cost not allocated. No depreciation outside common expense.

evidence.text:
[Passenger stats]
|Region|ASK m|RPK m|Passenger revenue m|Passenger direct cost m|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|Domestic|600|480|75|20|
|International|900|630|120|35|
[Cargo] Freight tonne-km 80m; cargo revenue 40m; direct cargo handling cost 12m. No standalone freighters; cargo in passenger aircraft belly.
[Shared costs] Common aircraft fuel/crew/lease cash expense 130m. Approved allocation 80% passenger,20% cargo. Passenger share allocated between regions by ASK. Central expense 15m unallocated.
[KPI] Passenger yield uses passenger revenue/RPK; network RASK includes all passenger/cargo revenue/ASK. Cargo contribution after allocated shared and handling costs.
[Draft] Sales assigns cargo full 40 revenue but no aircraft cost, labels cargo margin incremental; management assigns common cost twice to both passenger and cargo.
[Disclosure] No avoidable shared cost if cargo ceases, no aircraft weight limits.

qas.question: Find combined passenger load factor from region-level ASK/RPK.
Find international passenger yield per RPK.
Find domestic allocated share of common aircraft cost.
Find cargo segment result after allocated common cost.
Find consolidated operating result excluding double-counted allocations.
Why is a 28m cargo margin before allocated aircraft expense not the same as incremental cash benefit?
qas.answer: It excludes shared capacity costs and may differ from true avoidable/incremental costs; the case gives accounting allocation, not the cost of removing cargo.

qas.question: Why should the 130 common aircraft cost be counted only once in consolidated result?
qas.answer: Segment allocations partition the same expense; summing the allocations already captures 130m, so adding another full 130 double-counts.

qas.question: Can optimal aircraft cargo-versus-passenger capacity be calculated?
qas.answer: No. Payload limits, demand interaction and incremental operating costs are missing.

assumptions: Tỷ VND, nghìn tấn. Vườn hư cấu Lá Ngọc. Toy bearer trees PPE depreciated separately; harvested produce recognized at harvest value as inventory and production income. All cultivation costs expensed. No tax.

evidence.text:
[Orchard table]
|Block|Opening bearer PPE|Remaining life|Harvest kt|Harvest value triệu/tấn|Sold kt|Sales price triệu/tấn|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|East|200|10|12|5|10|7|
|West|160|8|8|4|7|6|
[Cultivation] Cash growing costs East45, West30. All harvested units enter inventory at stipulated harvest value; no opening inventory or losses.
[Expense] Packing/selling East8, West6; central cost10. No other costs, no impairment or revaluation of bearer plants.
[NRV] Ending East produce NRV6, West NRV3.5 triệu/tấn. Apply lower cost/NRV separately; write-down expense in P&L.
[Policy] Recognize harvest income at assigned value, then sales and related cost of sold inventory; do not count harvest value again as cash receipts.
[Draft] Manager revalues bearer trees to expected fruit sales and ignores West inventory write-down because East has higher NRV.

qas.question: Find current bearer-plant depreciation across both orchard blocks.
Find total harvest inventory addition at stipulated values.
Find external produce sales revenue.
Find ending produce inventory carrying after West NRV write-down.
Calculate total P&L including harvest income, sales, COGS, growing costs, D&A and write-down.
Why is bearer's tree carrying amount not replaced with the value of current fruit sales?
qas.answer: Bearer PPE and harvested produce are separate assets in the stipulated model; tree carrying follows depreciation, not sale value of annual fruit.

qas.question: Should East's higher NRV offset the West write-down?
qas.answer: No. Test ending produce separately by block; East cannot be written above cost to offset West loss.

qas.question: Can long-run orchard yield per hectare be compared across East and West?
qas.answer: No. Area and historical harvest data are not supplied.

assumptions: Tỷ VND. Trường giả lập Tầm Xuân. Toy grants earn reimbursement on eligible direct costs plus permitted overhead cap by sponsor. Cash received separately; ineligible direct cost university expense. No tax.

evidence.text:
[Grant ledger]
|Grant|Award ceiling|Direct spend|Ineligible portion|Overhead rate on eligible direct|Cash received|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|Alpha|100|70|10|20%|80|
|Beta|80|55|5|10%|50|
|Gamma|60|45|0|15%|60|
[Policy] Earned grant = eligible direct×(1+overhead rate), capped at award ceiling. Each grant separate; surplus cash refundable/unearned, undercollection receivable. No offset.
[Cost] Actual research overhead incurred 25 total across grants, not equal reimbursed overhead. All direct spend expensed; no other university P&L here.
[Opening] All grant AR/liabilities zero. No writeoff; award ceilings remain for future eligible costs.
[Draft] Manager claims full 240 award as revenue and nets grant receivable against refundable balances.
[Disclosure] No future spending plan or extension decisions.

qas.question: Find Alpha eligible direct cost and earned consideration; report earned amount.
Find Beta closing grant receivable.
Find Gamma refundable/unearned balance after current spending.
Find total gross grant liability across grants with excess cash.
Find total research operating result from grants after all actual direct and overhead costs.
Why does the full award ceiling 240 not equal earned grant income?
qas.answer: Awards are limits; recognition depends on verified eligible spending and permitted overhead. Unspent or ineligible portions do not earn reimbursement.

qas.question: Can Beta's 5 receivable offset Alpha and Gamma liabilities?
qas.answer: No. The grants have distinct sponsors/obligations and the toy explicitly prohibits offset.

qas.question: Can next year's total earned reimbursement be determined from unused award ceiling?
qas.answer: No. Actual future eligible expenditure, grant duration and sponsor decisions are absent.

assumptions: Triệu USD. Mỏ hư cấu Bấc Đá. Toy restricted rehabilitation fund is asset separate from closure provision; annual interest earned on fund, ARO unwind expense. Contributions transfer free cash, not expense; actual closure payments use fund and provision.

evidence.text:
[Rehab balances]
|Item|Opening|Current addition/revision|Interest/unwind|Cash paid for closure|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|Restricted fund asset|60|20 contribution|3 interest|10|
|Closure liability|100|15 upward revision|5 unwind|10|
[Policy] Revision15 relates to operating mine, capitalized as noncash PPE addition; no current depreciation on revision. Interest3 retained in fund; no other movement.
[Operations] Revenue 180, operating cost 110 cash, depreciation 20 existing assets. No other finance expense/tax.
[Cash] Opening unrestricted cash 40; operating receipts 175, operating cash cost110, contribution20 from unrestricted to fund. Closure payment10 made from fund. No capex cash or debt.
[Draft] CFO offsets restricted fund against closure liability, records contribution20 and closure settlement10 as new operating expenses, ignores unwind.
[Risk] No legal right of offset, no future closure cost/timing or fund investment risk data.

qas.question: Find ending restricted rehabilitation fund asset.
Find closing gross closure obligation.
Find net funding deficit as an analytical measure, not a balance-sheet offset.
Find PBT including fund interest and ARO unwind.
Find closing unrestricted cash.
Why is the 20 contribution not current operating expense?
qas.answer: It transfers unrestricted cash into a restricted fund asset; it does not extinguish closure obligation or consume resources externally.

qas.question: Why should 15 upward revision not be included in cash capex?
qas.answer: The toy capitalizes it through a noncash liability increase. No cash is paid on that revision date.

qas.question: Can the rehabilitation fund be considered fully adequate for eventual mine closure?
qas.answer: No. It is below the current modeled provision and future costs, timing and investment returns are uncertain.

assumptions: Tỷ VND. Tập đoàn giả lập Nguồn Tràm có generation and distribution wholly owned. Toy internal power purchases/sales eliminated; regulator-approved distribution tariff base not necessarily group external revenue. All output consumed same period.

evidence.text:

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|Generation|400|500|650|80|
|Distribution|1.000|0|780|50|
[Internal note] Generation bills distribution 500; full amount included in distribution 780 cost. No internal inventory or unsettled profit.
[Corporate] Central operating expense 60, interest 100, no tax. No other income/costs.
[Regulatory note] Distribution regulator recognizes internal purchased power 500 for tariff calculation, but consolidated P&L still eliminates it.
[Cash] Group external cash receipts1.350, external cash opex920 including central, interest100 cash, cash capex200. No other cash flows.
[Deck] Group sales 1.900 from both segments; CFO says internal tariff recognition makes elimination unnecessary.

qas.question: Find consolidated external revenue after elimination.
Find group operating cost before D&A including central after eliminating internal purchase.
Find consolidated EBITDA on the stated accrual cost base.
Find consolidated PBT after depreciation and interest.
Find cash generated after interest and cash capex using disclosed external flows.
Why does the tariff regulator's inclusion of 500 purchased power not override consolidation elimination?
qas.answer: The tariff calculation is a different regulatory scope; internal group transactions must still eliminate in consolidated reporting.

qas.question: Would eliminating internal revenue without matching distribution cost change profit incorrectly?
qas.answer: Yes. It would remove 500 revenue while retaining the same internal expense, understating consolidated result by 500.

qas.question: Can the generation segment's standalone return on capital be calculated?
qas.answer: No. The segment table provides profit flows but not invested capital or tax allocation.
